lessons.claim: Trump said US aid to Israel ($3.8B a year under the 10-year agreement) 'gets cut off at the end of the year' (Fox & Friends, Nov 3).
lessons.correction: Aid is leverage, not good will. It carries end-use rules, delivery review and the implied threat to slow shipments (Biden's 2,000-lb bomb hold, May 2024; Baker's loan-guarantee hold, 1991; Reagan's cluster-munition suspension, 1982). Cutting it while the US keeps underwriting the war (blockade, defensive strikes, missile-defense backing) unshackles Israel: more freedom to act, with the US still absorbing the consequences. Restraint factions claim a talking-point win but lose substance; Hawks and Netanyahu gain on substance. Tell missed: Netanyahu himself has pushed to phase out aid, and a recipient who wants to give up a benefit is telling you the benefit was a constraint.
lessons.generalRule: Before scoring winners, name the lever the act creates or removes and who holds it afterward; score fx by who gets the outcome, not who claims it.
lessons.mechanism: Removes a US brake (conditionality and supply leverage) without removing US exposure.
lessons.wrongReading: Cutting aid would help the restraint factions (Populists, Vance Lane), hurt the Hawks, and weaken Netanyahu's ability to pull the US into a wider Iran war.

lessons.claim: The ledger grouped a 'Populist-Nationalist Right' faction by its message ('no new wars') and scored members by it.
lessons.correction: Politicians and media figures wear a posture for their audience while their interests (patrons, holdings, career) differ. Verified Nov 3: Loomer backs the Iran war (Mar 3); Hawley voted against Iran war powers; Gabbard left citing family illness and defended the launch in office; Bannon told CPAC to back Trump (Mar 27); Thiel calls the war a mistake (Oct 12) while Palantir's Maven targeting use doubled; Vance was made by Thiel money ($15M, 2022) and the 1789 Capital circle, and keeps patrons and Trump's blessing whatever his talks posture. Also: claims about funding must be sourced; the reviewer's Carlson-Thiel and Bannon-Mercer links did not hold up as current (Carlson bought out 1789 Capital in Jun 2025; the Mercers cut Bannon off in 2017-18).
lessons.generalRule: Every person and faction stance has two layers: POSTURE (what they say, to whom, what it buys) and INTEREST (who pays or made them, what they own, what they lose if their stated position won). Assign membership and fx by interest and acts; label the gap explicitly.
lessons.mechanism: Factions are interest blocs held together by money, posts and audiences, not shared slogans.
lessons.wrongReading: Treated Loomer, Bannon, Carlson, Hawley, Gabbard and Kent as one anti-war bloc; left Thiel's Iran motive empty while Palantir (which he chairs) profits from the war; read Vance's Iran posture ('wants a deal') as his motive.

lessons.note: Worked examples of shallow readings the reviewer corrected. Analysts and the challenger read every entry before writing. The weekly auditor adds a lesson whenever a scored falsifier shows a reading was wrong.
